body.statement:
Suppose \(0<\lambda\le1\), so \(\kappa=\lambda\),
\(B^4\ge(Sd)^2\), and fix the class constants.  For every deterministic
exact design \(X=(X_{st})\), every interior reference path \(z_0\), and
every \(c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd}\), consider
the deterministic experiment \(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\) in
\texttt{def:fixed-design-induced-experiment}.  Its nearest-design estimator
satisfies
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \left[\{\widetilde\tau-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2\right]
 \le
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \left[\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2\right]
 \le C\left\{\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
          \vee D_X(z_0)^2\vee N^{-\lambda}\right\}.
\]
If \(\delta_0<1/2\), the last display is at most
\(CR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}(z_0,\Sigma)\).  If in addition
\(B^4>(Sd)^2\), then
\[
 cR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}(z_0,\Sigma)
 \le
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \left[\{\widetilde\tau-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2\right].
\]
Neither bound uses a lower local-modulus condition.

For every fixed admissible \(z_0\) and every
\(\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\), the conditional law under
\(\mathbb K_\xi\) given the exact design, with its labels, belongs to
\(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\) for \(\mathbb K_\xi\)-almost every design,
and \(\theta_{\mathfrak E}=\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\).  Consequently
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 \left[\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}
 -\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2\mid(X_{st})\right]
 \le C\left\{\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
          \vee D_X(z_0)^2\vee N^{-\lambda}\right\}
\]
for almost every design; under \(\delta_0<1/2\), its right side is at most
\(CR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\).  If every cohort design contains \(z_{0s}\)
exactly, the displayed risk is at most
\(C\{\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\vee N^{-\lambda}\}\), and
\(R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\le C\{\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\vee N^{-\lambda}\}\).
If instead \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\) for every cohort, then
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 \left[\{\widehat\tau-\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2
 \mid(X_{st})\right]\le CR_D,
 \qquad R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\le CR_D.
\]
No converse in terms of \(R_D\) is asserted.

For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), its labelled observed regular
conditional kernel belongs to \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) for
almost every admissible \(z_0\) under the marginal law of the query, and
\(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}=\tau(z_0)\) there by
\texttt{lem:causal-identification}.  Hence all preceding conditional upper
bounds transfer to \(P\) at those query values and at
\(P(\cdot\mid z_0)\)-almost every exact design; no conditional version at a
null query is selected.
body.justification: The theorem distinguishes the known-specification deterministic experiment from the outer unknown-query procedure and transfers its upper bounds through the labelled tuple \(\xi_P(z_0)\).
body.gap: Known Gaussian convex recovery and strong-convexity estimated-minimizer theory do not supply this bounded product experiment or its causal disintegration.
body.consumer: The marginal theorem combines its conditional mechanism with occupancy and outer rule-before-query witnesses.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(q=Sd\) and
\[
 A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s},
 \qquad D_X=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda.    \tag{1}
\]
Every \(n_s\) and \(\pi_s\) is positive, so \(A>0\).  First work in
\(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\).  In this experiment \(X,z_0,\Sigma\) are
known specifications; a decision rule may use them but is chosen before the
unknown labelled point \((\mathbb Q_\xi;\mu,f,z)\).

Conditional on the donors define
\[
 U_{si}=E_{si}-\mu_s-K_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_N}
 \{Q_{s,t_{s\ell},i}-f_s(X_{s,t_{s\ell}})\}.                \tag{2}
\]
Donor--history independence and independence of histories across \((s,i)\)
make these variables conditionally centered and independent across
\((s,i)\).  Boundedness gives \(|U_{si}|\le4B\), and therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb Q_\xi}\!\left(
 \sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}U_{si}
 \mathrel{\Big|}(Z_j)_j\right)\le16B^2A.                    \tag{3}
\]
Let \(t_s^0\) be the smallest nearest design index to \(z_{0s}\).  By the
definition of \(t_{s\ell}\) and two triangle inequalities,
\[
 \|X_{s,t_{s\ell}}-z_s\|_2
 \le\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})+\|z_s-z_{0s}\|_2
       +2\|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\|_2.                  \tag{4}
\]
Subadditivity of \(x^\lambda\) and Holder continuity imply
\[
 |f_s(X_{s,t_{s\ell}})-f_s(z_s)|
 \le C\{\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda+
 \|z_s-z_{0s}\|_2^\lambda+
 \|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\|_2^\lambda\}.              \tag{5}
\]
Projection onto the cube is nonexpansive, each balanced fold has size at
least \(N/3\), and \(\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)\le qC_\Sigma\).  Hence
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}\|\widetilde z_\ell-z\|_2^2
 \le\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)}{|I_\ell|}
 \le\frac{3qC_\Sigma}{N}.                                   \tag{6}
\]
The experiment also imposes \(\|z-z_0\|_2^2\le C_\Sigma/N\).  Expanding
\(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\) into the
centered sum in (3) and the approximation errors in (5), applying Jensen's
inequality to (6), and using \((x+y+z)^2\le3(x^2+y^2+z^2)\), gives
\[
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2
 \le C\{A+D_X^2+N^{-\lambda}\}.                            \tag{7}
\]
The estimator is measurable in the observations and known specifications
and does not use \((\mu,f,z)\); it is therefore an admissible minimax
witness.  Under \(\delta_0<1/2\), Lemma
\texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry} makes the right side at
most \(CR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\).

For later lower bounds, suppose two laws \(P_0,P_1\) have target separation
\(\Delta\) and total variation at most \(1-\eta\).  For
\(A_0=\{|\widetilde\theta-\theta_0|<\Delta/2\}\), the triangle inequality
shows that the squared error is at least \(\Delta^2/4\) under law one on
\(A_0\), and under law zero on \(A_0^c\).  Consequently
\[
 \max_{v=0,1}\mathbb E_v(\widetilde\theta-\theta_v)^2
 \ge\frac{\Delta^2}{8}\{P_0(A_0^c)+P_1(A_0)\}
 \ge\frac{\eta\Delta^2}{8}.                                 \tag{8}
\]

For the treated-mean channel take \(f_s=0\), \(Q_{sti}=0\), \(z=z_0\),
and fix the donor law.  Under \(v\in\{-1,1\}\), let the \(E_{si}\)'s be
independent with values \(\{-b,b\}\), where \(0<b<B\), and
\[
 \Pr_v(E_{si}=b)=\frac12+v\varepsilon_s,
 \qquad \varepsilon_s=\frac{\gamma\pi_s}{bn_s\sqrt A}.      \tag{9}
\]
Because \(A\ge\pi_s^2/n_s\), sufficiently small fixed \(\gamma\) puts all
probabilities in \([1/4,3/4]\).  The target separation is
\(4\gamma\sqrt A\), and the Hellinger affinity is
\[
 \prod_{s=1}^{S}(1-4\varepsilon_s^2)^{n_s/2}
 \ge \exp(-C\gamma^2/b^2)>0,                                \tag{10}
\]
since \(\sum_sn_s\varepsilon_s^2=\gamma^2/b^2\).  The
Cauchy--Schwarz affinity bound used in
\texttt{lem:full-covariance-location-pair} keeps total variation below one,
so (8) gives risk at least \(cA\).  The zero-displacement member of that
lemma supplies a donor law with the prescribed covariance; strict
fourth-moment slack guarantees membership.

For the fixed-design channel put
\[
 q_s(x)=a_0\min_{1\le t\le T}\|x-X_{st}\|_2^\lambda,
 \qquad f_s=q_s/2,\quad g_s=-q_s/2,                           \tag{11}
\]
with \(a_0\) small.  Lemma
\texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry} verifies that these
surfaces are admissible and coincide at all design sites.  Deterministic
zero responses, identical event laws, and identical donors therefore yield
identical observations, while the targets differ by \(a_0D_X\).  Equation
(8) with \(\eta=1\) yields risk at least \(cD_X^2\).

For the donor channel apply Lemma
\texttt{lem:full-covariance-location-pair}, choosing the displaced coordinate
in cohort \(s_0\).  Under both alternatives use the common surface
\[
 f_{s_0}(x)=a_1|x_k-z_{0,s_0k}|^\lambda,
 \qquad f_s(x)=0\quad(s\ne s_0),                             \tag{12}
\]
with \(a_1\) small enough for the Holder and support restrictions, and keep
the response and event laws identical.  If \(e\) is the displaced
coordinate, that lemma and ellipticity give
\[
 |z_{1,e}-z_{0,e}|
 =\frac{c_\eta N^{-1/2}}{\|\Sigma^{-1/2}e\|_2}
 \ge c_\eta c_\Sigma^{1/2}N^{-1/2}.                         \tag{13}
\]
The donor products have total variation at most \(1-\eta\), while (12)--(13)
separate targets by at least \(cN^{-\lambda/2}\).  Equation (8) gives risk
at least \(cN^{-\lambda}\).  The maximum of the three lower bounds and the
two-sided characterization in the rough-geometry lemma prove
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \{\widetilde\tau-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2
 \ge cR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}.                                   \tag{14}
\]

Now fix \(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Definition
\texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class} gives, conditionally on the exact
design, donor--panel independence, independence of histories across
\((s,i)\), and
\[
 \mathbb E[Q_{sti}\mid\mathcal X]=m_s(X_{st}),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]=\mu_s.      \tag{15}
\]
Thus for almost every design the conditional observed law, with its labels,
is the central point \(z=z_0\) of \(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\).  Bounded
responses give \(|m_s(X_{st})|\le B\) almost surely; the lower design-density
bound makes this true Lebesgue-almost everywhere, and Holder continuity
extends it to all \(x\).  Hence \(\|m_s\|_\infty\le B\), as required by the
experiment.  Its target is
\[
 \theta_{\mathfrak E}
 =\sum_s\pi_s\{\mu_s-m_s(z_{0s})\}
 =\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0).                            \tag{16}
\]
Applying (7) conditionally proves the nearest-design bound.  If every cohort
design contains \(z_{0s}\), then \(D_X=0\), and the exact-site risk and
modulus conclusions follow from (7) and the rough-geometry lemma.

Suppose instead \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\) for every \(s\).  Then
\((z_{0s},h_s^\star)\) is feasible in every foldwise anchor search, and
certificate optimality gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &C_H\|\widehat u_{s\ell}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
 +C_H\widehat h_{s\ell}^\lambda
 +C_V(Tn_s\widehat h_{s\ell}^d)^{-1/2}\\
 &\quad\le C_H\|z_{0s}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
 +C_H(h_s^\star)^\lambda
 +C_V\{Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d\}^{-1/2}.
 \end{aligned}                                               \tag{17}
\]
The bandwidth floor bounds the last term by a constant multiple of
\((h_s^\star)^\lambda\).  Since \(r=0\), Gram coercivity makes every fit
invertible and its intercept weights nonnegative with sum one; clipping is
therefore inactive for responses in \([-B,B]\).  Holder continuity bounds
approximation bias by the first two terms on the left of (17), while (15)
and whole-history independence give centered variance at most \(CA\).
Donor unbiasedness, projection contraction, and ellipticity give
\[
 \mathbb E\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^2\le3qC_\Sigma/N.     \tag{18}
\]
Jensen's inequality and (17)--(18) now yield
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [\{\widehat\tau-\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2
 \mid(X_{st})]\le CR_D.                                    \tag{19}
\]
The rough-geometry lemma also gives \(R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\le CR_D\).

Finally let \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\).  The corrected Lemma
\texttt{lem:panel-fixed-query-kernel-transfer} supplies, for
marginal-almost-every admissible query, the labelled point
\[
 \xi_P(z_0)=\bigl(\mathbb K_{P,z_0};\mu_P(z_0),m,
                         \Sigma_P(z_0)\bigr)
 \in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0),                         \tag{20}
\]
not membership of the bare kernel.  Lemma
\texttt{lem:causal-identification} gives
\(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi_P(z_0);z_0)=\tau(z_0)\) on the same conull set.
Equations (16)--(19) therefore transfer to the causal conditional problem at
those query values and at conditional-almost-every design.  The deterministic
subexperiment permits dependence on known \(X,z_0,\Sigma\), whereas the
feasible outer estimators are observable-data rules and do not receive the
unknown query.  No conditional version is selected at a query-null value.
